newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Poland could be in EU by 2000, Swedish PM says.
newsitem.headline: Poland could be in EU by 2000, Swedish PM says.

text.p: Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson, offering one of the most optimistic timetables to date for enlarging the European Union, said on Saturday Poland and other membership applicants may join by the year 2000.
"It is not an impossible target," he told reporters during a summit of European Union leaders in Dublin.
He was asked whether it was realistic to aim to bring in the first new members from central and eastern Europe and the Mediterranean before the year 2000.
Persson pointed out that Sweden had managed to become a member of the EU in three and a half years after the country decided to seek membership.
"It could (be possible) for the Poles as well, if we really want to," Persson said.
In a speech in Stockholm on Wednesday, Persson said it was his ambition that the EU would be able to welcome the first new members before 2000.
One of the main aims of the EU's current treaty review, known as the inter-governmental conference (IGC) and due to end in mid-1997, is to prepare the EU for up to 12 new members.
Membership negotiations are due to start six months after the conclusion of the IGC, which was the focus of discussions during the one-day summit in Dublin.
French President Jacques Chirac also said last month the target for Polish membership should be the year 2000.
However, officials at the European Commission, the EU executive, have raised doubts about such a timetable.

They say that it may just be possible to wrap up membership negotiations by the end of the year 2000 but the treaties would have to be ratified by all members states and applicants, a process which could take at least another year.
